reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes FastBNB as a way to deposit or stake BNB for stated daily returns, including a 3% figure, and provides instructions to purchase BNB, transfer it to MetaMask, and deposit it into the platform. It also associates referral activity with additional percentage-based earnings and discloses that linked products may generate a commission for the speaker, although the video includes a disclaimer that earnings are not guaranteed.

For FastBNB, you need BNB (Binance coin), so head over to Binance.us (or Crypto.com) and purchase as much as you are going to deposit into FastBNB
Wait for your purchase to clear and then withdraw your BNB to your MetaMask. Make sure to deposit to the BSC Network (Binance Smart Chain)
ox gives 3% daily and it's for 90 days
User can refer unlimited users under any level which way goes paying upto 10 Levels starting from 6% to a total of upto 18% unrestricted earing potentials

opening.argument: The video repeatedly frames its guidance as something viewers must evaluate for themselves, not as a guaranteed financial outcome. The presenter says to do their own research and consult a professional before making an investment decision, and the description says there is no guarantee of earnings and that the video is not financial advice. That caution matters when assessing the presentation: it warns viewers not to rely on the claims as assured results.

citations.quote: do your own research and also consult a professional investment advisor before you make any investment decision
There is no guarantee that you will earn any money using the techniques and ideas mentioned in this video.
This is not financial advice.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The stated returns are part of what the video discusses, but the cited 3% language alone does not establish that the presenter guarantees viewers will receive them. The opening also leaves out the video's explicit warning that results are not guaranteed and that viewers should do their own research. Those cautions do not prove the project is safe; they do weigh against treating the presentation as an unqualified promise.

citations.quote: There is no guarantee that you will earn any money using the techniques and ideas mentioned in this video.
do your own research

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer cannot erase the substance of the presentation. The video opens by inviting viewers interested in earning 3% daily to watch, describes an Ox plan at that rate, and gives steps for buying BNB and moving it to MetaMask for FastBNB. Saying earnings are not guaranteed does not change that the video promotes participation around stated returns.

opening.argument: The material is presented as a step-by-step guide and review, with substantial operational instruction about MetaMask, Binance Smart Chain, transactions, and withdrawals. The presenter describes checking contract analytics and comments, and shares personal account activity rather than simply asserting an outcome. Viewers are also told to evaluate the project and decide for themselves. That makes an educational demonstration a plausible reading of the video's primary role, even though it discusses a specific yield project.

all of these will help you judge is this a good investment for you or not. You have to make all of that decision yourself.
i'll show you the withdraw process for fast BNB

rebuttal.rebuttal: A tutorial title and a description of reviewing analytics do not, by themselves, establish that the video's central function is a neutral operational lesson. The cited material includes evaluation language, but it also directs viewers through participation in a named project and discusses its advertised daily yield. The tutorial framing should not be mistaken for proof that the investment claims have been independently validated.

Here are the steps to getting started with FastBNB

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational material is not detached from the investment pitch: the stated purpose is to get started with FastBNB, and the instructions include acquiring BNB and transferring it to the wallet for participation. The presenter also says the Ox plan pays 3% daily and recounts investing in it. Calling these steps a tutorial does not change their practical role in facilitating deposits into the promoted yield program.

opening.argument: The supplied material describes a cryptocurrency project and wallet workflow, but it does not establish from these records that the contract is fraudulent or that the presenter requests viewers' wallet credentials. The description identifies an affiliate commission as possible, openly discloses it, and says the presenter will not include products they have not verified or personally used. A referral feature or commercial interest warrants scrutiny, but neither alone proves deception; the records also do not independently verify the project's claims or establish its safety.

I won't put anything here that I haven't verified and/or personally used myself.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The visible MetaMask recovery-phrase warning concerns wallet security, not whether the promoted return scheme is legitimate. Likewise, disclosing a possible affiliate commission does not resolve the central concern: the video presents daily yields and describes referral income. The absence of a credential request is not enough to rebut promotion of a potentially deceptive investment mechanism.

citations.quote: User can refer unlimited users under any level which way goes paying upto 10 Levels starting from 6% to a total of upto 18% unrestricted earing potentials
ox gives 3% daily and it's for 90 days

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument properly concedes that the supplied records do not prove safety, but it also does not establish fraud merely by showing a yield program and referral terms. The affiliate disclosure is explicit, and the video tells viewers to assess the project, its facts, and its risks themselves. The wallet-security screen is ordinary setup guidance, not evidence of a request to surrender credentials.
